answer: Each agent earns an immutable reputation score recorded on the ivory ledger, incremented only when it signs a transaction with its unique cryptographic quill that timestamps the action. The score ages toward a zenith threshold, decaying quickly if the agent goes silent, so a newcomer must spend compute and stake tokens for each identity it creates to reach the same level. An attacker thus incurs a linear cost proportional to the number of fake identities, rendering large‑scale Sybil attacks infeasible.
